speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help us pinpoint the cause of your vision changes, can you tell me if the black spots are stationary or if they seem to move around with your eye movements? Also, have you noticed any pain in or around the eye, or any sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and the painless nature of your symptoms, I suspect a viral infection of the retina. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless vision loss and black spots in an AIDS patient with a history of severe opportunistic infections are highly suggestive of Cytomegalovirus retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis
